chronoseries.note: Sole node. No earlier or later chronospecies. The scale contrast is with centimetre-scale stromatolite cones of the same living mat, not with another species.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.pde: du/dt = Du laplacian(u) + f; dv/dt = Dv laplacian(v) + g
equations.steady_state: u_s = a + b, v_s = b / (a + b)^2
equations.onset_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.selected_wavenumber: k_star = argmax sigma(k), placed near 2 pi / lambda by the diffusivities, then shifted by the finite-amplitude factor 1.08 so the saturated field locks to the domain mode at 64.19 µm

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: a chemical system with diffusion can select a finite wavenumber.
Schnakenberg 1979: the two-species kinetics used here.
Petroff et al. 2010: living and ancient conical stromatolites have a centimetre-scale spacing set by diffusion and phototaxis. That spacing is not this slot's wavelength.
Shepard and Sumner 2010: gliding cyanobacterial filaments produce reticulate mats at a much larger scale than 64 µm.
Polerecky et al. 2009: pigments in microbial mats are spatially structured and can be mapped spectrally. This script does not reproduce their instrument.

specimen.note: Canonical gallery photograph of an extant cyanobacterial culture plate. Not a 64 µm micrograph. Paleoarchean CC-BY stromatolite photographs were rejected for age.

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion relation and the existence of a selected wavenumber
Reticulate mats from undirected filament motility (Shepard and Sumner 2010)
reconstructed_in_script: Diffusivities that place the saturated dominant Fourier mode at 64.19 µm
Equal-diffusion ablation, diffusivity sweep, eigenvector dispersion probe
Display transfer that paints activator peaks as beige colonies on an illuminated agar ground so the animation can be compared with the plate photograph
does_not_claim: That a published paper measured a 64.19 µm pigment wavelength in this mat
That the culture-plate photograph is a 64 µm field
That Petroff's cone equation is being solved
That colony-size distributions match (they do not; KS ≈ 0.45)
